habitat: Mainly larger towns, where it is tame. Flocks also use cliffs, mine shafts and farmland. It depends on human habitation.
summary: A common to abundant introduced resident. Highly variable in colour. It is a domestic breed descended from the Rock Dove of North Africa and Europe. Newman mentions pure white, white with a dark head, and dark grey with a white head, and many other combinations. The short line refers to green neck feathers. The call is coo-roo-coo. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Speckled Pigeon has red, white-spotted upperparts and a red face mask, and is not the variable town pigeon.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^4=16 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 8–32.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

viewNotes.note: A familiar town pigeon. Colour is too variable for one plumage to be stored.
The face colour was not fixed.
The back colour was not fixed. The short line mentions green neck feathers.

calls.description: coo-roo-coo. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Paris. The filename is COLLIV. No playable South African file was listed.
